metaDescription: Get online in Saudi Arabia with an eSIM on STC 5G, from $0.27/day. Install by scanning a QR code, keep your number for calls and texts, data only.
intro: This page helps you set up mobile data for your trip to Saudi Arabia using a travel eSIM. Plans are data-only, so your regular SIM stays in place for calls and texts. You install by scanning a QR code, then switch the line on when you arrive. Prices start from $0.27/day, with several data sizes to choose from.
countryContext: Saudi Arabia is a destination in the Middle East & North Africa region, and like anywhere, you will want mobile data ready the moment you land. Rather than searching for a local shop or relying on costly roaming, an eSIM has your data prepared in advance. In Saudi Arabia, that data runs on the STC network.
networkNotes: In Saudi Arabia, the eSIM connects through STC, the local mobile network it is provisioned on. Once your line is active, your phone selects the available signal automatically, the same way it would with a physical SIM. You do not need to choose a network manually or change any hardware.
connectionDetails: Choose a fixed bundle of 1, 3, 5, 10, or 20 GB, or an unlimited-daily plan giving 1 GB per day at full speed before the rate is reduced. Validity runs 3, 5, 7 or 30 days, from $0.27/day, and some plans support top-ups. The data covers maps, messaging, browsing, and internet calls.
activationNotes: You can install the eSIM over Wi-Fi before you leave home by scanning the QR code. Keep the line switched off until you reach Saudi Arabia, then turn it on. Most plans start on the first connection to a local network, so remember to enable data roaming on the eSIM line.
whyEsim: With an eSIM you skip the hunt for a SIM kiosk after landing in Saudi Arabia and avoid a surprise roaming bill from your home carrier. Your own number stays active for calls and texts, the data is set up before you fly, and there is no physical card to swap or lose.

faqs.q: Which network will my eSIM use in Saudi Arabia, and will my phone work?
faqs.a: The eSIMFlys eSIM connects through STC in Saudi Arabia. It works on eSIM-capable, carrier-unlocked phones — most iPhone XS and newer, Google Pixel 3 and newer, and Samsung Galaxy S20 and newer. Dial *#06# to check for an EID, which confirms your device supports eSIM.

faqs.q: When does my Saudi Arabia plan start?
faqs.a: Most plans begin when the eSIM first connects to a local network in Saudi Arabia, not at the moment of purchase. That means you can install it on Wi-Fi before you travel and it will start counting once you land and switch the line on.

faqs.q: Can I keep my own number while using the eSIM?
faqs.a: Yes. The eSIM is data-only, so your regular SIM stays active for calls and texts on your usual number. The eSIM simply handles your mobile data in Saudi Arabia. Just enable data roaming on the eSIM line so it can connect.

faqs.q: Which data size should I choose for Saudi Arabia?
faqs.a: It depends on your trip. Fixed bundles run from 1 GB up to 20 GB over 3, 5, 7 or 30 days, starting at $0.27/day, while an unlimited-daily plan gives 1 GB per day at full speed before the rate is reduced. Light users can start small; heavier use suits a larger tier or unlimited-daily. Some plans allow top-ups.
